title: Doc-friction section of `measure` repeats complaints that are already fixed
problem: 'Doc friction by file' quotes each file's latest reports with no sign of whether the file changed since. Process runs told to fix the named files spend the run rediscovering that the issue is gone.
evidence: 2026-10-17 process run sampled three 'latest' entries: promptctl.py BrokenPipeError on `measure | head` (main() wrapper already catches it, rc=0), validate requiring a done item's pr before the PR exists (prompts/promptctl.py:415 accepts "this"), land-your-work.md branch-recreation warning (line 81 already says it). All three were already fixed on main.
Source: python3 prompts/promptctl.py measure, 'Doc friction by file'
change: In measure, mark a report as possibly stale when its file has a commit newer than the report's date (git log -1 --format=%cs -- <file>), or drop it from 'latest'. One PR in promptctl.py with a unit test.
metric: share of 'latest' friction entries that still reproduce when a process run samples five
result: Partly helped (2026-10-25 re-sample of the six untagged 'latest' entries on CLAUDE.md, promptctl.py and prompt-1.md): 3 still real or informational, 2 stale because the fix landed in another file (platform/ci/check_post_frontmatter.py, wired in portfolio-validate.yml, answers the CLAUDE.md 'no CI guard' report; promptctl.py already prints a stderr notice for the slow measure), 1 a non-issue. The date tag cannot see fixes made elsewhere than the named file; a reader must grep before building on a report, as the section footer already says.

history.note: measure now prints "(file last changed D)" next to each friction file; simplest form of the change.

measure now tags each 'latest' report dated before its file's last change with [file changed since]; the file-level date alone was useless because every file changes daily. 61 of the current reports are tagged.
Verify pass: result written; no further tool change, since matching reports to fixes in other files would need guesses.
